key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current govern molten pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide welding optimization for low-thermal-expansion Invar molds used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool dynamics
Analysis of laser power, welding speed, and current effects
evidence_signal: Within the studied ranges, increasing laser power (5–6 kW) deepened penetration and promoted arc deflection; increasing speed (0.5–0.8 m/min) reduced penetration and width; increasing current (150–170 A) widened the weld and improved arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends over limited parameter ranges but provides no quantitative uncertainty or weld mechanical-property validation.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
